newsitem.title: FRANCE: Floods in north France kill four, disrupt traffic.
newsitem.headline: Floods in north France kill four, disrupt traffic.

text.p: Torrential rains and flooding hit the northern French city of Rouen overnight, killing four people, local officials said on Tuesday.
A 28-year-old woman and her two children aged three and seven were swept away by a mudslide near their home in the Rouen suburb of La Vaupaliere, officials said.
A motorist was killed in an accident in the city centre, blamed on poor visibility due to the heavy rainfall.
Roofs, trees and cars were damaged in the downpour and several dozen people were evacuated from their homes by helicopter during the night.
Some 10,000 homes in the area were without drinking water after waterpipes burst.
The railway line from Paris to the port city of Le Havre was out of service during the night but had resumed operation by the morning, the state railway company SNCF said.
Hundreds of cars were immobilised for several hours on the nearby A-15 and RN 15 highways between Rouen and the town of Yvetot to the west, but traffic was now moving freely, police said.
